test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 25 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the primary objective of the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act of 2006 in India?

options.text: To focus on large-scale industries only
To increase import tariffs to protect MSMEs
To promote and facilitate the development of MSMEs

solution:
The correct answer is __**To promote and facilitate the development of MSMEs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The primary objective of the MSMED Act, 2006 is to **promote and facilitate the development and competitiveness of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in India**.
 
• The Act provides the first-ever legal framework for the recognition of the concept of "enterprise", which comprises both manufacturing and service entities.
 
• It aims to address the policy issues affecting MSMEs as well as the coverage and investment ceiling of the sector.
 
• The Act also emphasizes on the **promotion of MSMEs through various schemes and incentives** to enhance their productivity and competitiveness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)**

 
 
• MSMEs are categorized based on their investment in plant and machinery or equipment and annual turnover.
 
• Micro enterprises: Investment up to Rs. 1 crore and turnover up to Rs. 5 crore.
 
• Small enterprises: Investment up to Rs. 10 crore and turnover up to Rs. 50 crore.
 
• Medium enterprises: Investment up to Rs. 50 crore and turnover up to Rs. 250 crore.
 
 
 
• **MSMED Act, 2006**
 
 
• The Act was enacted to address the diverse issues faced by the MSME sector and to promote its development.
 
• It provides for the establishment of a National Board for MSMEs to lay down policies and programs for the sector.
 
• The Act also includes provisions related to the delayed payments to MSMEs, aimed at ensuring timely payments and reducing financial stress on these enterprises.
 
 
 
• **Importance of MSMEs**
 
 
• MSMEs play a crucial role in the socio-economic development of India.
 
• They contribute significantly to the country's GDP, exports, and employment generation.
 
• MSMEs are vital for the balanced regional development of the country as they often operate in rural and semi-urban areas.
 
• The sector also fosters entrepreneurship and innovation.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for MSMEs**
 
 
• Various schemes and programs have been launched to support MSMEs, such as the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme, MUDRA Yojana, and the MSME Champions Scheme.
 
• The government has also implemented measures to improve ease of doing business for MSMEs, including simplifying registration processes and providing financial incentives.
